heading: Beta join — both directions are always O(1)
text:
### Beta join — both directions are always O(1) [LNLS.5.1]

Every beta node in a `linear_scan: false` program has its lmem_idx and
ralpha_idx join-key indexes always active, and — because LNLS.3.3
requires joining on the identity slot of `logical`-lifecycle schemas
— each index probe returns **exactly one candidate** (J_max = 1).

- `beta_right_activate(fact)` → **O(1)**: identity-slot probe via
  lmem_idx; exactly one left-memory token (if any) shares that key.
- `beta_left_activate(token)` → **O(1)**: identity-slot probe via
  ralpha_idx; exactly one right-alpha fact (if any) shares that key.
- `beta_right_retract(fact)` → **O(1)**: `right_idx` holds exactly
  one joined token per fact (J_max = 1).
- `beta_left_retract(token)` → **O(1)**: `ltok_idx` holds exactly
  one joined right fact per token (J_max = 1); no join tests needed.
- NOT-node equivalents: same O(1) guarantees via `ltok_idx` for
  `not_left_retract`.

The "fallback scan" code paths and the J_max iteration loops are
provably unreachable for any DSC compiled with `linear_scan: false`.  In a
dedicated `linear_scan: false` build configuration they may be stripped.

idris.name: lnls_5_1__at_most_one
idris.note: The candidate list has at most one member.

idris.name: lnls_5_1__extend_at_most_one
idris.note: Left-activation of an anchored node extends a token by at most one candidate: the clause's `beta_left_activate` in O(1).

idris.name: lnls_5_1__j_max_1
idris.note: J_MAX = 1: under a full-key anchor two candidates of a live memory joining one token are one fact -- the clause's `beta_left_activate` probe returns at most one.

idris.name: lnls_5_1__j_max_1_after_history
idris.note: THEOREM 5, closed at the top: after any history from a loaded network, at every node whose join test is a full-key anchor on an entity-lifecycle kind, every token joins at most one fact of the node's memory. The clause's left-activation half. Its right-activation half -- exactly one left-memory token per key -- needs every pattern of the prefix anchored, not only the right one: with a pattern of the prefix unconstrained by the anchor, tokens differing in that pattern share the key.

idris.name: lnls_5_1__j_max_1_engine
idris.note: At any engine with the view and one live fact per key, an anchored node's memory offers each token at most one candidate.

idris.name: lnls_5_1__j_max_1_singleton_after_history
idris.note: THEOREM 5, THE SINGLETON FORM: after any history of a program keyless for an entity-lifecycle kind, from keyless inputs, every token joins at most one fact of the node's memory, under any join test.
